definitions.explanation: A book or written work widely recognized as excellent or important. Refers specifically to written works, not art or music.

examples.japanese: これは{経済学|けいざいがく}の{名著|めいちょ}だ。
examples.english: This is a classic work of economics.

examples.japanese: {夏休|なつやす}みに{名著|めいちょ}を{読|よ}みたいと{思|おも}っている。
examples.english: I'm planning to read some classic books over summer vacation.

examples.japanese: {時代|じだい}を{超|こ}えて{読|よ}み{継|つ}がれている{名著|めいちょ}を{集|あつ}めたブックリストを{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made a book list of masterpieces that have been read across generations.

notes:
FORMATION:
{名|めい} (famous, excellent) + {著|ちょ} (book, written work). Part of the {名|めい}～ prefix family that denotes excellence.

RELATED {名|めい}～ COMPOUNDS:
- {名作|めいさく} (masterpiece — broader, includes films, art, etc.)
- {名曲|めいきょく} (famous piece of music)
- {名画|めいが} (famous painting; classic film)
- {名演|めいえん} (famous performance)

NUANCE:
{名著|めいちょ} is specifically for books and written works, while {名作|めいさく} can refer to any creative work.
